key_findings: **AchievementIdReceiver factory (FUN_007627A0)** is structurally identical to BCS-Y-1023 SendLogReceiver_HeapFactory: 184-byte SEH-wrapped wrapper with body alloc-check via FUN_009D1B35, conditional ctor via BCS-Y-1128, finalization via FUN_007945A0. Confirms the Receiver factory pattern generalizes across Pattern A receivers.

**VehicleGradeReceiver factory (FUN_0076CDD0) has a DISTINCT HYBRID shape** not seen in BCS-Y-1023 or BCS-Y-1144. 201-byte body with __thiscall(container, byte*) signature. Branches on container.byte[+0x50]: fast-path writes the grade byte directly to FUN_0076A3F0() return + 0xB8 (no receiver instantiation); slow-path runs the standard alloc + BCS-Y-1134 ctor + cleanup. The fast-path suggests VehicleGrade is special-cased with an inline cache byte at some target struct's +0xB8 - likely the actor's vehicle-grade inline field, applied directly when no command-queue context exists (the +0x50 flag).

**Both factories are dispatch-only**. Ghidra's Callers list is empty for both - they're reached EXCLUSIVELY via function-pointer table dispatch, same pattern as BCS-Y-1023. Likely registered in the Application::Lua::Script::Client::Command factory dispatch table (vftable_A at 0x00fdfb2c or vftable_B at 0x00fe02ac per evidence), but the calling slot is out of scope here.

**The hybrid factory shape opens a future question (deferred)**: is the fast-path/slow-path branch a per-receiver pattern variation (only VehicleGrade?), or a more general optimization (some receivers have inline-cache shortcuts for common state changes)? AchievementAchievedCountReceiver has a 16B instance with 3 fields (the structural anomaly) - its factory may also be hybrid. Currently no callers exist for it (BCS-Y-1131 is dead code), so no factory exists to catalog yet.
